title: Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objectives · deo270447-sec-0030-p1】The aim of this study was to describe the technical feasibility of rectal Flushing ESD. Video‐derived vessel and bleeding metrics were collected to characterize the procedural course and are reported descriptively.

【Background · deo270447-sec-0020-p1】Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is increasingly used for en bloc resection of large superficial colorectal lesions. Bleeding during ESD can interrupt the dissection plane, obscure visualization, require device exchange, and prolong the procedure. Techniques that improve visualization and facilitate controlled hemostasis may therefore be useful, particularly during dissection around visible submucosal vessels.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study Design, Setting and Participants · deo270447-sec-0050-p1】We conducted a retrospective descriptive video‐based case series of rectal ESD procedures performed using Flushing ESD. The study was conducted at St Mark's The National Bowel Hospital, London, United Kingdom, a tertiary referral center specializing in complex therapeutic lower gastrointestinal endoscopy.

【Study Design, Setting and Participants · deo270447-sec-0050-p2】The rectum was selected a priori as the initial setting for evaluating Flushing ESD because its relatively vascular submucosal plane provided a clinically relevant setting for descriptive assessment of bleeding‐related procedural events. Stable scope position and dependent fluid pooling with appropriate patient positioning also facilitated maintenance of a consistent saline immersion field.

evidence.text: We conducted a retrospective descriptive video‐based case series of rectal ESD procedures performed using Flushing ESD. The study was conducted at St Mark's The National Bowel Hospital, London, United Kingdom, a tertiary referral center specializing in complex therapeutic lower gastrointestinal endoscopy.

The rectum was selected a priori as the initial setting for evaluating Flushing ESD because its relatively vascular submucosal plane provided a clinically relevant setting for descriptive assessment of bleeding‐related procedural events. Stable scope position and dependent fluid pooling with appropriate patient positioning also facilitated maintenance of a consistent saline immersion field.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · deo270447-sec-0240-p1】In this small retrospective series, rectal Flushing ESD was technically feasible, with en bloc resection achieved in all 10 cases and all bleeding‐related events controlled endoscopically. These descriptive findings do not establish comparative hemostatic benefit and provide feasibility data to inform future prospective comparative studies.

【Principal Findings and Added Contribution · deo270447-sec-0190-p1】This retrospective video‐based series describes Flushing ESD at a European tertiary referral center. The technique was feasible in all included cases, with en bloc and R0 resection in all 10 procedures, while enabling systematic assessment of treated visible vessels, bleeding, red‐out episodes, and hemostatic instrument use.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · deo270447-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 (a) Depression of the blue pedal (1) activates electrosurgical energy delivery at (2) while simultaneously flushing saline through the channel to the knife tip (3). The parallel symbols (||) indicate that these events occur synchronously. (b) Proposed mechanism without saline flushing: micro‐bubbles may accumulate at the tissue interface, potentially promoting electrical spark discharge and local tissue injury. (c) Proposed mechanism with concurrent saline flushing: flushing may disperse micro‐bubbles, reduce spark discharge, and permit more controlled energy delivery to the target vessel.Figure 1 alt textSchematic illustration of flushing‐assisted saline immersion endoscopic submucosal dissection. Panel A shows foot‐pedal activation of electrosurgical energy with simultaneous saline irrigation through the knife channel to the knife tip. Panel B depicts the proposed mechanism without saline flushing, in which micro‐bubble accumulation may promote spark discharge at the tissue interface. Panel C depicts the hypothesized effect of concurrent saline flushing, which may disperse micro‐bubbles, reduce spark discharge, and permit more controlled energy delivery to the target vessel.

【TABLE 1 · deo270447-tbl-0001】TABLE 1 Patient, lesion, procedural, vascular, and hemostatic characteristics of the Flushing ESD cohort. Values are presented as number (%) or median (interquartile range), mean, as appropriate. Resection speed was calculated using the ellipse‐estimated area of the pinned resected specimen rather than directly measured specimen surface area. A visible submucosal vessel was counted when it was first subjected to electrosurgical treatment and was counted once only, irrespective of repeated treatment or subsequent reappearance. Intervention included pre‐coagulation, cutting, dissection, or any other electrosurgical application. Visible vessels that did not undergo electrosurgical treatment were not included. Treated vessels were classified as having a diameter greater than or equal to the 0.9‐mm knife ball tip, with larger treated vessels defined as those with a diameter greater than or equal to the 2.7‐mm shaft diameter. Bleeding‐related events and hemostatic forceps use are reported per procedure and normalized per treated visible vessel and per cm2 of resection area. ESD, endoscopic submucosal dissection; JNET, Japan NBI Expert Team; LST‐G MN, laterally spreading tumor, granular mixed nodular type; LST‐NG, laterally spreading tumor, non‐granular type; LGD, low‐grade dysplasia; HGD, high‐grade dysplasia; IQR, interquartile range; R0, histologically complete resection with negative horizontal and vertical margins; Paris 0‐Is, sessile protruding lesion; Paris 0‐Isp, subpedunculated lesion; Paris 0‐IIa+IIc, slightly elevated lesion with a depressed component.
